title: Verify the image signature in the pipeline and document the verify command
description: Add a final step to job build-push in .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml. It runs cosign verify and cosign verify-attestation against <repo>@<digest>, pinned to certificate identity https://github.com/OnFinance/mongodb-mcp-server/.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml@refs/heads/main (or the release tag ref pattern) and OIDC issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com, and fails the job if either check fails. Record the exact verify command and expected identity in the repository's release documentation (the Docker section of README.md in mongodb-mcp-server), so anyone pulling the image and the future admission policy use the same identity constraint.
acceptanceCriteria: docker-publish.yml contains a cosign verify step with both --certificate-identity (or --certificate-identity-regexp) and --certificate-oidc-issuer set. A test run in which the sign step is skipped makes the job fail at that verify step.
The mongodb-mcp-server README.md Docker section contains the cosign verify command with the certificate identity and OIDC issuer used by the pipeline

verificationMethod.description: Review the merged pull request: confirm the verify step runs after the sign and attest steps, uses the digest output rather than a tag, and pins the signer identity and issuer. Confirm the README documents the same command. Expected: all four hold, and the GitHub Actions log of the latest run shows 'Verified OK' from cosign.

rootCause.description: Even after signing, nothing in the release process checks the signature or states which signer identity is trusted, so a mis-scoped or missing signature would go unnoticed.
